manuscript.title: Transfer learning for early neuroinflammation detection from single-cell RNA-seq cohorts

abstract.summary: Transfer learning for early neuroinflammation detection from single-cell RNA-seq cohorts. We evaluate a transfer-learning workflow for identifying early neuroinflammation signatures from single-cell RNA-seq cohorts. The approach combines quality-control notebooks, graph-based clustering, and biomarker ranking to improve reproducibility across three public datasets.
keyFindings: We evaluate a transfer-learning workflow for identifying early neuroinflammation signatures from single-cell RNA-seq cohorts.
The approach combines quality-control notebooks, graph-based clustering, and biomarker ranking to improve reproducibility across three public datasets.
We test whether a reusable transfer-learning workflow can improve cross-cohort signal detection.
A preregistered notebook records preprocessing, clustering, and biomarker ranking steps.
implications: Reusable notebooks can reduce cross-cohort reproducibility friction.
Transfer learning may improve biomarker ranking when cohorts are small.
Reviewer trust depends on stronger statistics and release-ready data notes.
nextSteps: Add confidence intervals for the primary model comparison.
Publish the de-identified matrices and notebooks once review is complete.
Link biomarker claims to the recommended citation set.

executive.summary: Transfer learning for early neuroinflammation detection from single-cell RNA-seq cohorts evaluates a reusable workflow for earlier neuroinflammation detection. The main result improves F1 to 0.82, but the draft still needs stronger statistical reporting and data-availability detail before review.
